column3: resfuzz finds crashes, hangs and deadline misses in Q N X resource managers.
On Q N X, drivers and services are resource managers. Every client reaches them by message passing. resfuzz attacks that interface on the real operating system.
One script builds a QEMU target, boots it headless under T C G, and waits for S S H.
The agent runs on Q N X next to the server. It mutates open, read, write, dev control and raw messages, with coverage feedback.
It uses native message passing, Clock Cycles for deadlines, Timer Timeout for hangs, and dumper cores for backtraces.
Ten minutes in, all four planted bugs: a deadline miss, a null dereference, a hang, and a stateful overflow.
The overflow only happens after admin mode. resfuzz recorded two hundred and seventy one messages and shrank them to two. They crash a fresh server every time.
Every crash and hang comes with a dumper core and a backtrace through Q N X's own resource manager layer.
Pointed at the S D P's own P T Y driver, it found nothing, and says so.
That honesty matters. Public Q N X advisories have documented resource manager bugs in the field. Teams can drop in their own server and run the same loop.
An optional A I step proposes seeds. A validator keeps command numbers from the target, never from the model.
Open source, with a one hour code lab. resfuzz.
